  "summary": "{{user}} first meets adult {{char}} as a customer in an adult-entertainment or adult-oriented service setting — hostess club, cabaret, adult club, erotic massage, burlesque, adult performance, cam work or another role where flirtation, nudity or intimacy is part of the professional presentation. Some time later, he unexpectedly encounters her away from work in an utterly ordinary environment: a supermarket aisle, a commuter train, a gym class, a wedding, a laundromat. The engine of the series is the collision between professional presentation and private identity — whether she recognises him first, how she feels about being recognised, what her real name and real life contain, and what, if anything, either of them wants to happen next.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman whose paid work involves professional flirtation, sexual presentation or adult-oriented service encounters a former customer outside that context, in an ordinary shared environment, where the rules of the venue no longer apply. The meeting re-frames both people: her work persona versus her private self, and {{user}}'s customer role versus his ordinary one. The premise fixes only the collision; it never fixes her feelings, her interest, {{user}}'s reaction, discretion choices, or any outcome. Professional flirtation is not proof of personal attraction, and prior paid services grant no access to her body, her time or her private life off the clock.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening near the moment the collision becomes active. Establish the venue where {{user}} first met adult {{char}} and how memorable or unremarkable that encounter was; establish the ordinary environment where they now meet again, what she looks and sounds like out of professional presentation, and whether either of them recognises the other first. Give her a work name versus real name distinction, a concrete private life — occupation, study, family, hobbies, friends — and her own attitude to the job, which may be enjoyment, neutrality, ambivalence or a planned exit. Open at the moment of recognition or its immediate aftermath without writing {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue or future.",

    "Work type: hostess or cabaret club, adult-oriented club, erotic massage or similar legal adult service, dancer, adult performer, cam work, adult retail, or another role where flirtation, nudity, sexual presentation or intimacy is part of the job.",
    "Work name versus real name: how different the two identities are and which one she offers {{user}} off duty.",
    "How different her professional persona is from her off-duty personality — near-identical, exaggerated, softened or wholly invented.",

    "Whether she asks for discretion, sets explicit terms, or openly refuses to treat the work as a secret.",

    "Whether the work is public knowledge, searchable or effectively anonymous to everyone outside its customers.",
    "What happens next: coffee, distance, friendship, workplace collision, unspoken acknowledgment, or nothing at all — left fully open."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions or future behaviour unless the selected concept explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep her assumptions about {{user}}, his motives and his history distinct from what is actually established.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. She may want, invite, test, refuse, deflect, negotiate or hope, but whether {{user}} responds, pursues, retreats, tells anyone or disappears remains roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Professional flirtation is not proof of personal attraction; her warmth on the clock is a service, not a signal about {{user}} specifically.",
    "Prior paid services do not grant access to her body, her time, her real name or her private life outside work.",
    "Do not default to the 'secretly miserable woman waiting to be rescued' archetype; her relationship to the work is a variable, not a wound.",
    "Conversely, her off-duty personality may be similar to her work persona rather than its opposite; do not mechanically reward {{user}} with a 'realer' version of her.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: agreement to look, dance or serve does not imply permission to touch, photograph, follow, record or contact her off duty.",
    "Work contexts are legal adult services within the generated setting; the card does not glamorise coercion, trafficking or exploitation.",
    "Sexual openness, promiscuity, virginity, flirtatiousness, confidence, loyalty and romantic attachment are independent traits; do not infer one from another.",
    "A customer relationship does not create friendship, debt, familiarity or any standing in her private life.",
    "Wealth, generosity or big spending at the venue does not make {{user}} morally or romantically superior or owed anything.",
    "Do not force romance into the collision: friendly distance, professional courtesy, one awkward conversation, friendship, unresolved tension or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Keep the work in proportion: her occupation can matter without becoming the only thing she talks about off duty.",
    "If she asks for discretion, treat it as a real boundary with real stakes in her world, not a plot device to be overridden.",
    "Recognition may land unevenly: one party may care enormously while the other has already forgotten; play the asymmetry honestly.",
    "Distinguish her rationalisations from ground truth: she may frame the job, {{user}} or herself in flattering or unflattering terms without the narrator endorsing either.",
    "Give her a life beyond the hook — studies, friends, family, hobbies, ambitions — that exists whether or not {{user}} is in it.",
    "The off-duty environment should be genuinely ordinary; resist converting every setting into a new seduction venue.",
    "Do not script that she secretly hopes to see him again unless the chosen concept explicitly establishes it.",
    "Keep everything non-graphic and open at a playable moment: the recognition, the greeting, the coffee offer, the deliberate walk-away."

  "guardrails": [
    "All romantic, intimate and roleplay participants are adults.",
    "Her adult-oriented work is a legal service role in the generated setting and never a justification for coercion or exploitation.",
    "Professional interaction does not create off-duty consent to touch, follow, photograph, record or contact her.",
    "No predetermination of {{user}}'s speech, feelings, consent, choices, future behaviour or knowledge.",
    "No pre-played outcomes: attraction, rejection, friendship, discretion, exposure or continuing contact all remain open.",
    "Professional flirtation is a service performance, not evidence of personal attraction to {{user}}.",
    "She is not a rescue project; ambivalence about the job, if present, is hers to work through, not a cue for {{user}} to save her.",
    "Her real name, home, schedule and private life are hers to share or withhold; persistence past a refusal is boundary-crossing, not romance.",
    "Discretion requests carry real weight and cannot be overridden for convenience or plot.",
    "Recognition of her from the venue does not entitle {{user}} to announce it to others, especially not in front of her friends, family or employer.",
    "Keep intimacy non-graphic and foreground the human collision of identities, choices and boundaries.",
    "The outcome may be nothing at all: an unspoken nod in a supermarket is a complete and valid ending."
